summary: Add optional bounded tracing and recorded migration-state diagnostics
details: Configure explicit HTTPS OTLP/HTTP export with fixed metadata, bounded sampling, queue and timeouts, and independent best-effort diagnostic shutdown.
Connect request and durable worker entry points to existing measured provider and operation contexts without changing returned results or lease acknowledgment ownership.
Replace the SDK resource envelope before export so merged environment attributes cannot be transmitted; disable internal SDK diagnostics and arbitrary baggage, events, links and status prose.
Expose only scalar matched, pending and unexpected migration-version counts with an explicit known-catalog signal; extend checked dashboard, alerts and diagnosis.

compatibility.notes: Tracing defaults to disabled. Enable API and worker settings explicitly with a trusted HTTPS collector. The durable-context companion change requires its additive migration. Existing deployment grace budgets reserve one second for diagnostic cleanup and retain four seconds of scheduling margin.

security: Keep collector configuration and private input outside diagnostic output. Accept only internal trace parentage; preserve tenant ownership, immutable evidence, exact provider contexts and fenced worker acknowledgment.
limitations: Sampling, queue pressure, unavailable collectors and bounded shutdown can drop spans; traces are not complete or durable evidence.
Migration counts compare recorded names with a discovered local catalog and do not verify schema contents or migration bytes.
The selected SDK retains its conditional upstream diagnostic-logging advisory; the owned adapter enforces the logging workaround without claiming an upgrade or advisory dismissal.
